de.PAGE_TITLE: Vierzehn Skills. Ein guter nächster Schritt.
de.DESCRIPTION: Vierzehn Agent-Workflows für Codex und Claude Code. Finde den passenden Skill und wähle Koch-Namen oder einfache Fragen.
de.HEADLINE: Dein nächster Schritt, gut vorbereitet.
de.INTRO: Cookbook by Pengusto ist eine Sammlung von vierzehn Agent-Skills. Sie helfen dir und deinen Agents, Projekte gezielt zu starten, Arbeit zu prüfen und Ergebnisse sauber zu übergeben.
de.HERO_ALT: Grünes Cookbook mit Pfanne und Spiegelei – das Motiv der Skill-Sammlung.
de.SKILLS_CAPTION: Vierzehn Skills. Jeder hat seinen Platz.
de.NAMING_HINT: Dieselben vierzehn Abläufe. Wähle die Namen, die zu dir passen.
de.HOW_TITLE: Vom richtigen Moment zum nächsten Schritt.
de.STEP1_TEXT: Projektstart, unklarer Fortschritt, Review oder Abschluss? Öffne den Skill, der zu deiner aktuellen Frage passt.
de.STEP2_TEXT: Koch-Namen oder einfache Fragen: Du installierst eine Variante. Die Inhalte und Werkzeuge sind identisch.
de.STEP3_TEXT: Installiere für Codex oder Claude Code, rufe den Skill auf und prüfe die Ergebnisse. Offene Fragen und Freigaben bleiben sichtbar.
de.INSTALL_TITLE: Einmal auswählen. In deiner Umgebung nutzen.
de.INSTALL_INTRO: Für Codex reichen zwei Befehle. Für Claude Code und die Offline-Installation stehen geprüfte ZIPs bereit. Du installierst vierzehn Skills in einer Namenswelt.
de.EXTRACT: ZIP vollständig mit versteckten Ordnern entpacken. Im Terminal in den äußeren Ordner cookbook-by-pengusto wechseln, dann:
de.NEW_SESSION: Danach eine neue Host-Sitzung starten. Die jeweilige CLI muss installiert und angemeldet sein.
de.UPDATES_TEXT: Ein neues ZIP ersetzt keine aktive Installation automatisch. Sichere die bisherige Paketkopie und installiere die aktualisierte Version über die Plugin-Verwaltung deines Hosts neu. Im Cookbook-Repo: git pull --ff-only und python3 scripts/launch_check.py.
de.SWITCH_TEXT: Nur eine Namenswelt pro Host aktivieren. Beim Wechsel das bisherige Cookbook-Plugin sichern und deinstallieren, nur seinen Marketplace abmelden und den neuen Paketordner registrieren. Alte Einzelkopien oder vibe-coding-cookbook zuerst bewusst ablösen, damit keine doppelten Skills entstehen.
de.LANG_NOTE: Die Website gibt es auf Deutsch und Englisch. Skill-Namen und Aufruf-IDs bleiben stabil; die Skill-Anleitungen werden dadurch nicht automatisch übersetzt.
de.ABOUT_TEXT: Von Pengusto für die Arbeit mit Agents: vierzehn gezielte Workflows aus einer gemeinsamen Quelle. Die Skills geben Orientierung, machen Prüfungen nachvollziehbar und lassen Entscheidungen bei dir. Das abgebildete Kochbuch ist ein Markenmotiv, kein physisches Produkt.
de.STATUS_TEXT: Öffentliche Beta 0.6.0 mit vierzehn Workflows. Paket- und portable Build-Prüfungen; frühere Abnahmen sind versionsgebunden dokumentiert. Keine Store-Freigabe und kein Sicherheits- oder Rechtsversprechen.
de.PRIVACY: Ohne Tracking, externe Fonts oder eingebettete Dienste. Cookbook und Skills mit MIT-Lizenzen.
de.REMOTE_INSTALL: Codex direkt aus dem geprüften GitHub-Marketplace installieren. Kein Entpacken nötig:

en.PAGE_TITLE: Fourteen skills. A good next step.
en.DESCRIPTION: Fourteen agent workflows for Codex and Claude Code. Find the right skill and choose Kitchen names or Plain questions.
en.HEADLINE: Your next step, well prepared.
en.INTRO: Cookbook by Pengusto is a collection of fourteen agent skills. They help you and your agents start projects with purpose, review your work and hand over clear results.
en.HERO_ALT: Green Cookbook with a frying pan and fried egg, the visual identity of the skill collection.
en.SKILLS_CAPTION: Fourteen skills. Each has its place.
en.NAMING_HINT: The same fourteen workflows. Choose the names that work for you.
en.FOOT_NOTE: Clear workflows. Results you can review.
en.HOW_TITLE: From the right moment to the next step.
en.STEP1_TEXT: Starting a project, checking progress, reviewing or wrapping up? Open the skill that matches your current question.
en.STEP2_TEXT: Kitchen names or Plain questions: install one variant. Both contain the same workflow instructions and tools.
en.STEP3_TEXT: Install for Codex or Claude Code, invoke the skill and review the results. Open questions and approvals stay explicit.
en.INSTALL_TITLE: Choose once. Use in your environment.
en.INSTALL_INTRO: Codex takes two commands. Verified ZIPs are available for Claude Code and offline installation. Install fourteen skills in one naming style.
en.EXTRACT: Extract the complete ZIP, including hidden folders. In your terminal, enter the outer cookbook-by-pengusto folder, then run:
en.NEW_SESSION: Then start a new host session. The corresponding CLI must be installed and signed in.
en.UPDATES_TITLE: Already installed? Updates and switching variants
en.UPDATES_TEXT: A new ZIP does not automatically replace an active installation. Keep a copy of the previous package and reinstall the updated version using your host’s plugin manager. In the Cookbook repository: git pull --ff-only and python3 scripts/launch_check.py.
en.SWITCH_TEXT: Enable only one naming style per host. When switching, keep a backup, uninstall the previous Cookbook plugin, remove only its marketplace and register the new package folder. Deliberately replace older standalone copies or vibe-coding-cookbook first to avoid duplicate skills.
en.LANG_NOTE: The website is available in German and English. Skill names and invocation IDs remain stable; switching website language does not translate the skill instructions.
en.ABOUT_TEXT: Built by Pengusto for working with agents: fourteen focused workflows maintained in one shared source. The skills guide your work, make checks traceable and keep decisions in your hands. The pictured cookbook is a brand illustration, not a physical product.
en.STATUS_TEXT: Public Beta 0.6.0 with fourteen workflows. Package and portable-build checks; earlier acceptance records are version-specific. No store approval or security/legal certification.
en.PRIVACY: No tracking, external fonts or embedded services. Cookbook and skills carry MIT licenses.

start-it-right.summary: Start small: turn an idea into the next verifiable project step.
start-it-right.when: You have an idea but need a concrete first step.
start-it-right.ingredients: A product idea or repository, audience, constraints and existing conventions. No account access required.
start-it-right.steps: Understand the project, resolve only necessary choices and implement the authorized slice without mandatory tickets.
start-it-right.verify: The next step has an observable outcome; open decisions stay explicit.
start-it-right.result: A compact project starting point with recommendations and, when confirmed, useful artifacts.
start-it-right.limits: Extra modules and tracking are optional. Brainstorming does not authorize implementation; existing approval is retained.

are-we-cooking.summary: Briefly check whether the current approach serves the goal.
are-we-cooking.when: Many attempts, unclear progress or a suspected detour.
are-we-cooking.ingredients: The current conversation, agreed goal, relevant results and checks.
are-we-cooking.steps: Compare the known goal, evidenced progress and main obstacle; recommend the next useful decision.
are-we-cooking.verify: Cooking, Stalled, Side quest or Unclear is supported by evidence.
are-we-cooking.result: A brief course correction and next step.
are-we-cooking.limits: Diagnosis alone does not authorize new changes. Historical pattern analysis is optional.

did-i-leak.summary: Review the working tree and Git history for sensitive content and coverage gaps.
did-i-leak.when: Before sharing a repository or preparing to make it public.
did-i-leak.ingredients: A Git repository, Python 3 and Git. Gitleaks and TruffleHog are optional; coverage stays explicit.
did-i-leak.steps: Run a redacted scan; assess findings, missing scanners and unreadable files.
did-i-leak.verify: Working tree and reachable history are covered; missing scanners and remaining checks are documented.
did-i-leak.result: GO, GO WITH REVIEW or NO-GO, with concrete reasons.
did-i-leak.limits: No proof of complete security. No credential rotation, history rewrites or publication without approval.

will-they-sue-me.summary: Review a specific product flow or launch for evidence-backed gaps.
will-they-sue-me.when: An app or website needs a technical review before launch or after changes.
will-they-sue-me.ingredients: Repository, real data flows, operator and markets; browser and test data; current primary sources for legal claims.
will-they-sue-me.steps: Set review depth, trace relevant flows and obligations, and propose scoped fixes with acceptance checks.
will-they-sue-me.verify: Each finding has evidence, a basis, a review date and acceptance criteria; unknown applicability stays open.
will-they-sue-me.result: A prioritized review table and concrete remaining questions.
will-they-sue-me.limits: No legally safe or lawsuit-proof promise; no real payments, deletions or external actions for testing.

let-them-see-it.summary: Make a repository shareable with suitable documentation and a verified installation.
let-them-see-it.when: The product works locally but documentation, installation or release boundaries are missing.
let-them-see-it.ingredients: Repository, Git status, installation flow, existing documentation and licenses.
let-them-see-it.steps: Evaluate first, implement relevant authorized changes and avoid mandatory languages or generic file lists.
let-them-see-it.verify: Quickstart and package agree; local, committed, pushed and deployed remain distinct.
let-them-see-it.result: A reviewable repository with explicit publication gates.
let-them-see-it.limits: Preparation does not authorize publication. Clarify new licenses and scope; avoid a blanket file checklist.

what-did-we-change.summary: Write change notes that distinguish releases, fixes and uncommitted work.
what-did-we-change.when: A version or first release needs understandable change notes.
what-did-we-change.ingredients: Git repository, target ref and suitable base ref or first release; GitHub access is optional.
what-did-we-change.steps: Justify target and base, clarify ambiguity and accurately describe evidenced changes and repaired regressions.
what-did-we-change.verify: Every claim is supported by the selected changes; versions and verification status are accurate.
what-did-we-change.result: Release notes as text, without publication.
what-did-we-change.limits: Invoking the skill does not authorize tags, releases or file changes. Omit claims without reliable evidence.

kill-the-todos.summary: Close a chat briefly with evidence, or pause with a deliberate handoff.
kill-the-todos.when: The current conversation should wind down, end or be continued later.
kill-the-todos.ingredients: The agreed goal, existing results, open work and relevant checks.
kill-the-todos.steps: Reuse existing checks, finish authorized remaining work and briefly state completion, open work and any needed re-entry.
kill-the-todos.verify: Completed work has evidence; open, deferred and blocked items remain visible.
kill-the-todos.result: A verified finish or concrete handover with a way to resume.
kill-the-todos.limits: Guide-only and pause modes do not change files or task status. No blind TODO completion, publishing or automatic archiving.

what-was-i-cooking.summary: After a pause, recover the goal, current state and open work.
what-was-i-cooking.when: After a break or a long conversation, the agreed goal, completed work or open items are unclear.
what-was-i-cooking.ingredients: Available history of this conversation, later goal decisions and verified outcomes.
what-was-i-cooking.steps: Reconcile goals and later decisions, recap briefly and identify missing history.
what-was-i-cooking.verify: Approved goal changes are distinguished from suggestions; missing history and unverified outcomes stay explicit.
what-was-i-cooking.result: A compact recap of the current state and a useful next step.
what-was-i-cooking.limits: Recap only: no file edits, task-status changes, automations or automatic resumption of remaining work.

here-we-go-again.summary: Inspect recurring failures and recommendations without follow-through.
here-we-go-again.when: When attempts repeat or accepted recommendations remain unfinished.
here-we-go-again.ingredients: Relevant history, artifacts and verified outcomes within the agreed scope.
here-we-go-again.steps: Bound the evidence; identify causes; reconcile advice; propose prevention.
here-we-go-again.verify: Every pattern has a source; single incidents and hypotheses remain distinct.
here-we-go-again.result: A ranked retrospective with recommendation status and a checkable improvement.
here-we-go-again.limits: A report alone does not authorize fixes, rule edits, tickets or reminders.

catch-me-up.summary: Return to a project after a long break with current context.
catch-me-up.when: When goals, decisions and the current state need refreshing.
catch-me-up.ingredients: Available chat, handoff and relevant current project artifacts.
catch-me-up.steps: Recover the last agreed state; check relevant current facts; explain changes; recommend a reentry point.
catch-me-up.verify: Old reports and current checks remain separate; missing history stays visible.
catch-me-up.result: A compact project reentry with purpose, decisions, today’s state and one next step.
catch-me-up.limits: Do not resume implementation automatically or infer current deployment from old claims.

finish-my-prompt.summary: Complete a partial prompt using visible context.
finish-my-prompt.when: When autocomplete is unavailable or a sentence is unfinished.
finish-my-prompt.ingredients: Prompt fragment, visible context, intended outcome and existing limits.
finish-my-prompt.steps: Read the draft; preserve intent; fill the gap; return a copyable suggestion.
finish-my-prompt.verify: No invented facts or expanded scope; the proposed prompt is not executed.
finish-my-prompt.result: An editable complete prompt or the requested suffix only.
finish-my-prompt.limits: Manual drafting fallback; no native Tab integration or exact autocomplete-model claim.

which-name-wins.summary: Find fitting names and compare Plain/Kitchen pairs together.
which-name-wins.when: When a product or skill needs a name or a consistent name pair.
which-name-wins.ingredients: Purpose, audience, tone and relevant existing names; no private corpus required.
which-name-wins.steps: Understand the use moment; create pairs; check collisions; recommend a choice.
which-name-wins.verify: Both variants name the same capability; choices remain distinct from suggestions.
which-name-wins.result: Ranked pairs with both invocation IDs and a short rationale.
which-name-wins.limits: No unverified availability claim and no renaming inferred from a question.

explain-the-cookbook.summary: Understand Cookbook, choose a fitting skill and invoke it correctly.
explain-the-cookbook.when: When getting started or unsure which workflow fits your situation.
explain-the-cookbook.ingredients: Available skills, installed naming style, your question and desired result.
explain-the-cookbook.steps: Explain the collection; distinguish similar purposes; recommend a skill; show its invocation.
explain-the-cookbook.verify: Only available invocations are presented as installed; display names and IDs remain distinct.
explain-the-cookbook.result: Clear orientation, one fitting recommendation and an editable example.
explain-the-cookbook.limits: Explains and recommends; no automatic execution, installation or approval.

you-got-this.summary: Turn a project goal into a complete, verified result autonomously.
you-got-this.when: The goal is set and you want the agent to investigate and own implementation.
you-got-this.ingredients: Project goal, repository conventions, available tools and observable quality criteria.
you-got-this.steps: Trace the actual flow; set a quality bar; implement the smallest complete change; verify and critique the integrated result.
you-got-this.verify: The result meets the quality bar; tests, observed behavior and unverified gates remain distinct.
you-got-this.result: A reviewable implementation with evidence, limitations and a useful handoff.
you-got-this.limits: Audit remains read-only unless fixes are requested. Delegation does not authorize publication, destructive changes or additional cost.
